status_reason: The concept cannot be approved: the existing Vis-NIR silica cable cannot carry MIR, and an approval of any alternative needs the fiber type, link length, routing and conditions, which are not supplied.
answer: No, the concept cannot be approved as stated: the existing silica cable transmits about 350–2400 nm, while MIR ATR starts at 4000 cm-1 (2.5 µm) and the AFS water-in-petroleum example spans 4000–2000 cm-1, so MIR needs CIR or PIR fiber. AFS has a published MIR ATR example for water in petroleum with ZrO2 or diamond ATR tips, which makes MIR ATR the method to test first in the laboratory, but the sources document no MIR fiber reach comparable to the 100–300 m silica cables, so an analyzer in another building must be confirmed by AFS. NIR over low-OH silica, which supports long remote links and covers moisture bands, is the alternative to compare.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR with a ZrO2 or diamond ATR probe on CIR fiber in the laboratory on the client's oil with known water additions, and compare against NIR over low-OH silica.
inline.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 (or diamond) tip sealed in a PEEK shaft
inline.install: Laboratory first; later in contact with the oil in the petroleum line at a point still to be defined
inline.fiber: Chalcogenide As-S (CIR, 1.1–6.5 µm), not the existing Vis-NIR silica cable
inline.test_against: NIR transmission/transflection probe on low-OH silica fiber
inline.not_final_because: The existing silica cable cannot carry MIR, no MIR fiber reach to another building is documented, and the water range, link length, routing and process conditions are not supplied.

problems.text: The existing visible/NIR silica cable transmits only about 350–2400 nm, but MIR starts at 4000 cm-1 = 2.5 µm and the water-in-oil ATR spectra span 4000–2000 cm-1, so MIR ATR needs CIR (1.1–6.5 µm) or PIR (3–17 µm) fiber.

Long 100–300 m cables are documented only for low-OH silica (Vis-NIR), while the mid-IR fiber comparison is shown only for 2 m, so AFS must confirm whether any MIR link to another building is feasible.
Approval is asked before the facts allow it: fiber type, link length, routing and operating conditions are not supplied, and method selection depends on such factors.
The AFS water-in-petroleum slide gives no detection limit, fiber link length or process conditions, so it is a reason to test MIR ATR, not proof it works in this line.

methods.why: AFS shows MIR ATR spectra of oil with 0.1–2.0 % water where absorbance increases with water content, and ATR suits liquids with a 1–6 µm sampling depth.
NIR covers moisture bands (1.3–2.2 µm), works with ordinary silica optics and remote probes, and low-OH silica supports 100–300 m links, so it may fit the existing cable and distant analyzer.
Raman runs on silica fibers in the visible/NIR and carries information complementary to MIR, but organic samples can mask it with fluorescence.
Fluorimetry relies on secondary emission of certain substances and has low selectivity, so it is not a direct route to water content.

questions.q: What is the distance and cable routing between the measurement point on the petroleum line and the analyzer building?
questions.why: Long links are documented only for silica (Vis-NIR) and MIR fiber reach must be confirmed.

questions.q: What water content range do you expect and what accuracy do you need?
questions.why: The AFS example covers 0.1–2.0 % water and calibration samples must span your range.

questions.q: What are the temperature, pressure, flow, cleaning and hazardous-area conditions at the intended probe location?
questions.why: Probe and fiber choice depend on the conditions, which are not supplied.

questions.q: Which independent laboratory method do you use today to determine water in this oil?
questions.why: A chemometric model must be built and validated against independent reference values.

technical.spectral_window: MIR ATR 4000–2000 cm-1 (2.5–5 µm) per the AFS example, carried by CIR fiber (1.1–6.5 µm); PIR (3–17 µm) covers only 3333–2000 cm-1 of it; the existing Vis-NIR silica (350–2400 nm) suits only the NIR alternative.
technical.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 or diamond tip sealed in a PEEK shaft, in direct contact with the liquid (sampling depth 1–6 µm); path length for an NIR probe unknown – ask.
technical.fiber: CIR or PIR for MIR, length and routing unknown – ask; existing silica cable from a visible or NIR setup only usable for NIR.
technical.sampling: Measurement point on the petroleum line, sampling rate and response time unknown – ask.
technical.reference_method: unknown – ask (independent laboratory water determination on the same samples).
technical.calibration: Oil samples with known water additions spanning the client's range (AFS example used 0 %, 0.1 %, 0.5 %, 1.0 % and 2.0 %), with a built and validated chemometric model.

experiment.objective: Establish in the laboratory whether MIR ATR, and alternatively NIR, sees water content differences in the client's own oil.
steps: Obtain client oil samples and prepare a water-addition series covering the client's expected range.
Record MIR ATR spectra with a ZrO2 or diamond ATR probe on CIR fiber and NIR transmission/transflection spectra on silica fiber for each sample.
Determine water content of every sample with the client's independent laboratory reference method.
Select key spectral features and build and validate chemometric models for each method on the same samples.
Have AFS confirm whether a MIR fiber link of the required length is feasible; otherwise evaluate NIR over low-OH silica for the remote link.
references: Independent laboratory water determination on each sample (method unknown – ask)
experiment.go_no_go: Accuracy and range criteria must come from the client.

pathway.key_features: No client spectra yet; the AFS example shows MIR absorbance in 4000–2000 cm-1 increasing with water content from 0.1 to 2.0 %.
pathway.path_reason: Lab trials and key-feature selection come before choosing a chemometric model, customised system or sensor.

multispectral.why: Raman and MIR carry complementary vibrational information and a combi ATR probe with CIR and silica fibers exists, but for a single water target with a direct MIR ATR example a combination is only worth testing if the best single method fails.
multispectral.test: Only if pursued, the fused model must beat the best single method on the same validation data.

assumptions: The oil at the measurement point is a liquid suitable for ATR contact.
The client's water range is unknown and assumed comparable to the 0.1–2.0 % AFS example only for planning the first sample series.
